newsitem.title: NORWAY: FOCUS-Sun shines as Kvaerner posts Q1.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Sun shines as Kvaerner posts Q1.

text.p: Shares in Norwegian construction and engineering company Kvaerner ASA surged seven percent on Friday in hefty turnover after the group reported first quarter results beating market expectations.

Analysts said the much-needed turnaround had come earlier than expected but results in the second quarter -- one year after the acquisition of British conglomerate Trafalgar House Plc -- would show whether a positive trend in the core businesses had materialised.

London-headquartered Kvaerner booked a first-quarter operating profit of 442 million crowns ($62.5 million), against 593 million crowns a year ago, and a pre-tax profit of 224 million crowns versus 537 million crowns.
The comparative figures are adjusted to take into consideration the Trafalgar House takeover.
Kvaerner said it was disappointed with its result in the first quarter, but it expected to improve full-year operating profits compared with 1996.

"Our first quarter results are lower than we wanted them to be, although we still anticipate a much better operating profit in 1997 compared with 1996," Erik Tonseth, Kvaerner's president and chief executive, told a news conference.

Analysts, however, reacted positively to the figures and Kvaerner's share price on the Oslo bourse surged to a high soon after the open of business at 392 crowns in the A stock and 362 crowns in the Bs.
At 1155 GMT the A share was 23 crowns up at 381 crowns, while the B was 21 crowns up at 350 crowns.

"They caught us by surprise this morning," said an Oslo-based analyst. "It looks like many of the contracts that they were losing on last year they have either completed -- particularly in oil and gas -- or sufficiently provisioned for in the fourth quarter.

"We're already beginning to see profits from new contracts. The improvement has come earlier than expected but I think it is going to strengthen throughout the year and in that case I see a share price of 450 (crowns) at least."
Analysts said shipbuilding continued to provide good results while Kvaerner's oil and gas division showed a surprisingly strong result.
First quarter profits before tax for shipbuilding amounted to 256 million crowns, versus 283 million crowns. Kvaerner said it expected the division to show a satisfactory result.
Oil and gas posted pre-tax profits of 67 million crowns against 69 million crowns in the year-ago period and a loss of 32 million crowns of the full-year 1996.
New contracts in oil and gas in the first three months totalled 12.5 billion crowns and the order reserve increased by 77 percent to 20.9 billion crowns.
The company's languishing pulp and paper business improved performance from a year ago booking a pre-tax loss of 26 million crowns compared with a loss of 37 million in the 1996 period.
"The continued losses are due to a low business volume, rather than the contract problems which were experienced in 1996," Kvaerner said.

"Pulp and paper is expected to have a strong improvement in results compared to last year, but the strength of that improvement is dependent on the business area winning some significant projects which are now being progressed."

Kvaerner said asset sales in the second quarter, including its 17 percent stake in Norwegian shipping group Bergesen d.y. Group and its holding in British rival Amec Plc, had achieved its objective to divest 10 billion crowns of non-core assets following the Trafalgar buyout.
Proceeds from these sales will be used to reduce the group's interest bearing debt, which in turn will enhance future pre-tax profits, Kvaerner said. ($ = 7.069 Norwegian Crowns)
